title: Certificate for the three adic condensed coefficient families
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$. A sheaf $\Lambda$ of abelian groups on profinite sets, together with its specified commutative monoid-object structure, has the certificate $\mathrm{IsEllAdicCoefficient}(\ell,\Lambda)$ if it is exactly one of the following ring objects [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring; sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]: (i) the continuous-function condensed ring $C(-,E)$ for a finite normed extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$; (ii) $C(-,\mathcal O_E)$ for a finite extension $E\subseteq\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ with the induced valuation; (iii) $C(-,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$. The certificate is the inductive proposition with these three constructors and no others. Both the underlying sheaf and the monoid-object structure are indices, so a different multiplication on the same sheaf is not certified.

proof.text: Use one constructor for each displayed coefficient family, indexed by its actual continuous-function ring object and its canonical multiplication. There are no further constructors. This records the three cases without choosing any data from an unproved existence assertion.
